subject: Renewal: Horizon AI - term uplift & surge capacity review
messages:
From: Alex Green <alex.green@horizonai.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@horizonai.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion + Q2 usage pack attached

Hi Hannah —

Attaching our Q2 usage report and a short note on where we are seeing spikes. Renewal window opens in three weeks and we want to make sure we lock terms that reflect our new usage patterns. Quick highlights:
- Aggregate token consumption up 78% QoQ driven by a new real-time personalization stream.
- Average request latency is within SLA but 95th percentile bursts during peak hours are causing occasional throttles.
- Cost per 1k tokens has become a gating factor for forecasts; procurement asked for a couple of term scenarios.

Can your team put together a short plan with (a) recommended commit uplift, (b) optional surge credits, and (c) any performance/ops steps to reduce 95th pct jitter? I attached the usage report (RI-2028-Q2-usage-report.pdf).

Thanks,
Alex Green
Head of Platform
Horizon AI

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@horizonai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Aug 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion + Q2 usage pack attached

Alex —

Thanks for the report; we pulled it into our renewal model and sketched three options. High level first pass:
- Scenario A (Rightsize): +40% commit, keeps same term, includes 1.5x burst credits for peak days.
- Scenario B (Uplift + Perf): +65% commit, 12-month term, dedicated routing during peak windows (cost uplift) — targets cutting 95th-pct bursts by ~35%.
- Scenario C (Aggressive Upsell): +120% commit, 24-month term, deeper pricing tiers and a 10% overage buffer.

I'll have Marcus and Monica attach the quantitative sheets with token economics and latency projection this afternoon. Are you available Monday for a 30-min review with procurement?

—Hannah
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Aug 2028 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal discussion + Q2 usage pack attached

Linking the modeling output — see attached "Horizon-Uplift-Scenario.xlsx" (sheets: current_run, scenario_A, scenario_B, scenario_C). Key assumptions in the sheet: token mix (generation vs embed) unchanged, average sequence length increased 12%, and estimated savings from persistent KV caching when applicable.

Summary numbers (annualized):
- Scenario A: ARR delta +$135k, unit price -7% effective
- Scenario B: ARR delta +$210k, unit price -12% effective, estimated infra uplift cost +$25k/yr for dedicated peak routing
- Scenario C: ARR delta +$390k, unit price -18% effective, services uplift for migration +$45k one-time

Operational asks to hit Scenario B numbers: enable scheduled dedicated routing 2–6pm PT M–F and provision an extra 1.25 p90 capacity buffer for the first 90 days.

-Marcus
Senior Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

On Fri, Aug 10, 2028 at 11:03 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Alex —
> 
> Thanks for the report; we pulled it into our renewal model and sketched three options. High level first pass:
> - Scenario A (Rightsize): +40% commit, keeps same term, includes 1.5x burst credits for peak days.
> - Scenario B (Uplift + Perf): +65% commit, 12-month term, dedicated routing during peak windows (cost uplift) — targets cutting 95th-pct bursts by ~35%.
> - Scenario C (Aggressive Upsell): +120% commit, 24-month term, deeper pricing tiers and a 10% overage buffer.

Thanks — this is helpful. Procurement wants to understand the SLA tradeoffs for Scenario B before committing to the term change. A couple of questions:
1) Can you quantify the expected 95th pct latency improvement in ms for the dedicated routing?
2) How would surge credits work operationally (apply automatically vs. manual claim)?
3) Do you have a sample contract language for the 12-month amendment (we aim to avoid long legal cycles).

We can do Monday at 2pm PT for a quick run-through. I looped procurement.

—Alex

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@horizonai.com>, procurement@horizonai.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Aug 2028 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion + Q2 usage pack attached

Alex / team —

Appreciate the quick turn. Answers below and attaching a 1-page amendment template for the 12-month term.

1) 95th pct improvement: based on recent regressions and our dedicated routing tests, we expect a median reduction of ~45–60ms and a 95th-pct reduction of ~120–200ms under current peak profiles when dedicated routing + KV-prefix caching are applied. Exact numbers depend on sequence-length mix; we included a sensitivity tab in the workbook.

2) Surge credits: we recommend an automatic applied model for 1.5x burst credits that trigger when daily peak consumption exceeds the committed corridor. Credits reconcile monthly and apply as a discount against overage lines — no manual claim required. We can toggle to a manual claim workflow if procurement prefers verification steps.

3) Contract language: attached "Redwood-12mo-Amendment-sample.docx" (one-pager) — it covers commit uplift, burst credit mechanics, and SLA targets for peak routing. Legal has pre-approved this for expedited signature but can accept small customer edits.

Next steps: 1) confirm Monday 2pm PT (we'll send calendar invite), 2) procurement to flag any mandatory contract edits before the call, 3) we will prepare a short ops runbook for the first 90 days including activation steps for dedicated routing and verification checks.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood-12mo-Amendment-sample.docx
